title: Rolling Upgrade Impulse Controller and Migration Planner for Private Deployments
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary: Implement the 'Impulse Controller' service and accompanying Migration Planner to orchestrate rolling upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers. The goal is an opinionated, auditable, and reversible upgrade flow that supports: LTS channel adherence, staged rollouts, automated schema/data migrations, compatibility gating, and safe rollbacks for on-prem and VPC deployments.

Scope:
- Impulse Controller: a coordinator that executes rollout plans as ordered waves. Responsibilities include wave scheduling, per-node pre-checks, drain/evacuate, orchestrated migration jobs, KV cache warm-up hooks, post-upgrade validations, and automatic rollback when critical checks fail.
- Migration Planner: generates per-customer upgrade plans given current cluster topology, pinned model versions, storage topology (stateful components), and allowed LTS channel policy. Outputs include ordered waves, required migration jobs (DB/schema, config transforms), estimated downtime windows, and a rollback strategy.
- Gates & Policies: implement canary gating (configurable percent + region waves), compatibility matrix checks (agent version <-> server runtime <-> model artifacts), and safety thresholds (error rate, latency, disk pressure).
- Orchestrated Migrations: standardize migration job runbook for Postgres/etcd-like state, schema-versioned migrations with idempotency guarantees, and a dry-run mode for previewing effects.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Staggered wave vs big-bang: we prioritize staggered waves with adaptive concurrency. Trade-off: longer overall upgrade time but significantly lower blast radius and easier rollback.
- Central coordinator vs fully decentralized agents: we selected a central Impulse Controller that issues signed step tokens to agents. Rationale: simpler global decisioning for complex safety checks and easier audit logging. We accepted the operational need to harden the controller (rate-limit, HA via leader-election).
- Schema migration approach: require idempotent versioned migrations executed as separate jobs rather than inline on agent start. Trade-off: additional orchestration complexity but higher safety for stateful upgrades.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated rollout can perform a full upgrade on a 3-region test cluster with canary (5%) + 25% + 70% waves and automatically stop & rollback when post-upgrade validation fails.
- Migration Planner can produce a deterministic plan for clusters with heterogeneous node roles and output a human-readable runbook.
- Audit logs produced for each step with timestamps, actor (system or operator), and decision reason.
- Integration tests for: compatibility matrix enforcement, dry-run migrations, rollback correctness, and KV cache warmup validation.
- Runbook and on-call playbook published in Confluence; GitHub Actions to run dry-runs against a staging backend.

Non-goals:
- Replacing customer-specific custom migration scripts. We provide hooks and a migration runner but customers keep final control over bespoke heavy-data transforms.

Rollout plan (implementation phases):
1) Design & safety review (done) — produce Sequence Diagram, compatibility matrix schema, and conformance tests.
2) Minimal controller prototype + planner (wave scheduling + dry-run) — target internal staging.
3) Migrations runner + idempotent migration library + agent hooks.
4) SRE/QA chaos testing + scalability tests.
5) Beta rollout to selected Private customers with explicit opt-in and observed SLO metrics.

Notes on observability: controller emits per-step metrics (step_duration_seconds, failures_total), plan hashes for traceability, and per-customer audit events exported to existing Console ingestion pipelines.

2026-02-23 | Avery Coleman (Infra): Reviewed approach — asked for HA leader election pattern and how tokens are signed for step authorization. Recommended using existing leader-election library and JWT-signed step tokens.
2026-02-28 | Lin Zhou (SRE): Raised concern about disk pressure threshold being too permissive; requested adding a hard cap that blocks upgrades when disk_usage_percent > 85%.
2026-03-03 | Priya Kapoor (PM): Confirmed customer beta tranche (3 customers) and requested customer-facing opt-in flow in Console. Action: add a release label and a short UI acceptance checkbox.

2026-03-05 | Maya Stein: Prototype controller merged to infra branch (PR 2189). Basic wave execution + dry-run works in staging. Observed a race where two controllers attempted the same plan; added leader lock and retry backoff (see PR notes).
2026-03-08 | QA: Ran migration dry-run on staging cluster. Found an idempotency bug in a migration script when re-run after failure; created ENG-45174 to track migration library fix.
